prospects.thesis: HII is the sole builder of U.S. nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and one of two Virginia-class submarine prime contractors, giving it a durable moat tied to multi-decade Navy shipbuilding budgets. The combination of positive 1M momentum (+4.2%) against a weak defense tape, cheap P/S of 0.9x, and bullish options + institutional flow signals suggests smart money is accumulating ahead of FY27 defense appropriations. Shipbuilding backlog visibility plus Mission Technologies growth (unmanned/AI) make this a high-conviction defense pick.

RTX offers diversified exposure across missile defense (Raytheon), military engines (Pratt & Whitney), and avionics (Collins), benefiting directly from elevated munitions replenishment demand tied to ongoing geopolitical conflicts. Bullish options and institutional positioning combined with a flat 1M print provide a stable entry while peers sold off. Near-term catalysts include continued Patriot/NASAMS orders and GTF engine inspection progress unlocking margin recovery in 2027.

Leidos is a top IT services/digital modernization prime for DoD and intelligence agencies, differentiating from hardware-heavy peers via software, AI analytics, and cyber. The -8.2% 1M drawdown creates an attractive entry at just 0.9x sales with bullish options and institutional accumulation signaling the selloff is overdone. Catalysts include ramping Sentinel/CJADC2 adjacent work and continued federal AI/cyber spending tailwinds.

Lockheed's -7.7% 1M pullback offers a rare discount on the world's largest defense prime, with F-35 sustainment, PAC-3/THAAD missile defense, and space systems providing multi-year revenue visibility. Bullish options flow and institutional buying into weakness suggest the post-earnings selloff is being absorbed. Munitions replenishment orders and potential Golden Dome-style missile defense initiatives are near-term catalysts.

Qualcomm provides essential theme diversification away from pure defense, with leadership in smartphone modems plus accelerating traction in automotive (Snapdragon Digital Chassis) and edge AI PC chips (Snapdragon X). The -8.2% 1M drawdown reflects Apple modem-loss fears that are already priced in, while bullish options and institutional signals point to recognition of the AI-at-the-edge pivot. 4.1x P/S remains reasonable versus semi peers with auto/IoT segments posting double-digit growth.
